title: Compressor keeps tripping at the warehouse

dispatch.complaint: Last guy said the compressor is going bad. We want a second opinion before we spend five grand.
dispatch.notes: Previous tech's note: 'Comp 1 tripping on internal OL. Recommend replace.'

faults.description: Compressor 1 sees only two phases. Locked-rotor amps on two legs.
Internal overload trips on heat from single-phase locked-rotor current.

readings.txt_tstat: BAS: occupied, Y1 and Y2 called. Space 79°F.
readings.txt_controller: M2: compressor 1 output on. Compressor 2 running. ⚠ M2 alarm list shows compressor 1 trips; exact code not verified against Lennox docs.
readings.txt_look_unit: Compressor 1 hums loudly for a few seconds, then goes quiet. Compressor 2 running normally.
readings.txt_look_electrical: K1 pulled in. L1 pole contact face burned and cratered. Discoloration on the L1 load lug.
readings.txt_look_condenser: Coil clean, fans running (compressor 2 still carrying load).

hints: Did anybody check what's feeding the compressor?

diagnosis.label: K1 L1 pole burned open → single-phasing → internal overload trips
diagnosis.feedback: Root cause found. Balanced line voltage, 398 V across a 'closed' pole, 0 A on L1.

diagnosis.label: Compressor 1 failing (bad windings)
diagnosis.feedback: Windings are balanced at 1.9 Ω and megger is clean. The compressor's a victim, not the cause.

diagnosis.label: Utility phase loss
diagnosis.feedback: Line voltage is balanced at the disconnect. The leg is lost after K1.

diagnosis.label: Bad internal overload
diagnosis.feedback: It's doing its job. Locked rotor on two legs will trip anything.

diagnosis.label: M2 board cycling the compressor
diagnosis.feedback: M2 output stays on. The compressor trips on its own protection.

repair.label: Replace K1, let the compressor cool, verify balanced amps
repair.feedback: Compressor starts clean, three balanced legs. You just saved them a compressor.

repair.label: Replace compressor 1 (previous tech's call)
repair.feedback: New compressor, same burned K1. It'll single-phase and trip again, maybe cook the new one.

repair.label: Let the overload reset and leave
repair.feedback: It'll trip again within the hour.

repair.label: Replace both K1 and compressor 1
repair.feedback: Fixed, but the compressor tested good. That's a $4,800 part they didn't need.

idealPath.why: Hums then trips. Not a dead compressor; something's starving it.
Balanced supply. Problem is inside the unit.
398 V across the L1 pole: that pole isn't making contact.
Lock out before you ohm windings.
Balanced windings, clean megger. Compressor's healthy.

debrief: The previous tech found a symptom (internal overload) and called it a cause. Single-phasing at locked-rotor amps will trip any healthy overload. On a 460 V unit, an open pole back-fed through the motor windings reads about 1.5x phase voltage (~398 V) across the contacts. Balanced supply plus a big drop across one pole puts the fault in the contactor. Always check what feeds a compressor before condemning it.
